title: Macroscopic Quantum Interference of the Center-of-Mass Motion of Levitated Superconducting Microparticles enabled by Magnetic Higher-Order Traps
authors: Jaume Cunill-Subiranas, Fabian Resare, Suocheng Zhao, Sofia Qvarfort, A. Metelmann, Carles Navau, Witlef Wieczorek
abstract: We show how magnetostatic higher-order multipole traps can be used to generate macroscopic quantum interference of the motion of levitated superconducting microparticles. An appropriate combination of multipolar magnetic fields offers great versatility in constructing various trap potentials, including anharmonic trap potentials such as Duffing or double-well types. Crucially, the anharmonic trap potentials realize a nonlinearity on the order of hundred times the zero-point motion, i.e., on a length scale below nanometers. These anharmonic potentials allow for the generation of quantum features of the center-of-mass motion of a magnetically levitated superconducting microparticle. Importantly, they can be easily generated with a static arrangement of coils, requiring only that the current running through them is tunable. We propose protocols exploiting the versatility of the magnetic trap landscape to generate non-Gaussian motional states. We solve the dynamics of the center-of-mass motion of the particle in phase space and analyze its parameter dependence. Furthermore, we give a recipe to distinguish classical from quantum behavior in a statistically meaningful way through measurement of the position of the particle. Our results open a path to accessing the quantum regime of the center-of-mass motion of objects with masses larger than picogram, i.e., $10^{13}$ atomic mass units. This will enable fundamental physics experiments for studying the transition between quantum and classical behavior, exploring the intersection between quantum physics and gravity as well as probing of certain types of dark matter.
summary: This paper demonstrates how magnetic higher-order traps can confine superconducting microparticles to generate anharmonic potentials necessary for observing macroscopic quantum interference. By controlling the trap landscape using static coils, researchers can manipulate the center-of-mass motion into non-Gaussian states. This opens a new experimental avenue to test fundamental physics questions regarding the quantum-classical transition with massive objects.
main_problem: The research aims to generate and study macroscopic quantum interference effects in the center-of-mass motion of levitated superconducting microparticles.
main_result: The use of magnetic higher-order traps allows for generating non-Gaussian motional states, opening a path to fundamental experiments studying the quantum-to-classical transition with masses exceeding picograms.
method: The authors analyze the dynamics in phase space using anharmonic potentials (like Duffing or double-well types) derived from magnetostatic higher-order traps. They also provide protocols for distinguishing classical from quantum behavior via position measurements.
model_or_system: The system involves superconducting microparticles levitated by magnetic fields, where the trapping potential is engineered using static arrangements of coils to create anharmonic potentials (e.g., hexapole terms). The dynamics are modeled in phase space, sometimes utilizing a Wigner function approach for analysis.
key_observables: Non-Gaussian motional states, position measurement statistics used to distinguish classical vs. quantum behavior.
important_parameters: Masses larger than picogram ($10^{13}$ atomic mass units), anharmonicity realized on sub-nanometer length scales.
main_assumptions: The analysis often relies on the small-sphere approximation for simplifying the complex potential calculation, although general field generation is discussed.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates various magnetic traps (harmonic and anharmonic) for superconducting particles using coil configurations and resulting potentials (e.g., double-well).
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical platform (superconducting levitation), details the theoretical tool (HOTs generating anharmonic potentials), proposes protocols to generate nonclassical states, analyzes the dynamics in phase space, and concludes with experimental feasibility for fundamental tests.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses quantum mechanics at macroscopic scales using a clean, controllable physical system (superconductors) and advanced trapping techniques, which is highly relevant to AMO physics concerning quantum measurement and decoherence.
